messages.subject: Vet Business Weekly: Private equity clinics hit 28% of market
messages.body:
VET BUSINESS WEEKLY
April 2, 2026

→ INDUSTRY CONSOLIDATION ACCELERATES
Corporate-owned veterinary practices now represent 28% of the U.S. market, up from 25% in Q4 2025. Mars Veterinary Health and National Veterinary Associates lead acquisitions in the Pacific Northwest and Southeast regions.

→ STAFFING CRISIS DEEPENS
AVMA reports 15,000 unfilled veterinary technician positions nationwide. Average sign-on bonuses have increased to $3,200 for credentialed techs in urban markets.

→ SCHEDULING SOFTWARE ADOPTION
67% of independent practices now use digital scheduling, up from 52% last year. Primary driver: client expectation for online booking.

Read more at vetbusinessweekly.com

messages.body:

messages.subject: Vet Business Weekly: Burnout survey results released
messages.body:
VET BUSINESS WEEKLY
May 21, 2026

→ VETERINARIAN BURNOUT AT ALL-TIME HIGH
AVMA study: 78% of veterinarians report symptoms of burnout, with administrative tasks cited as top non-clinical stressor. Time spent on records, billing, and scheduling averages 12 hours per week.

→ WHAT CORPORATE GROUPS OFFER
Acquired practices report reduced admin burden but loss of clinical autonomy. 61% of selling practice owners stay for contracted period then leave profession.

→ PRICING PRESSURE
Independent practices face price compression on routine services while cost of goods increases 7% year-over-year.

messages.subject: Vet Business Weekly: The real reason practices sell
messages.body:
VET BUSINESS WEEKLY
June 11, 2026

→ WHY OWNERS SELL TO CORPORATE
Exit interviews with 50 selling practice owners: 67% cite administrative burden as primary factor, ahead of retirement (52%) and financial opportunity (48%). Many report spending more time on operations than medicine.

→ INDEPENDENT PRACTICE ADVANTAGES
Long-term client relationships remain competitive moat. Practices with 10+ year client relationships show 2.3x higher lifetime value.

→ TECH STACK REALITY CHECK
Practices running 4+ separate systems (scheduling, records, billing, client communication) report highest staff frustration and error rates.
